steps.title: Import TypeScript types and utilities
steps.instruction: Import the TypeScript types and utilities that will be used throughout the lesson. Add the following imports at the top of your file: `type`, `interface`, `Record`, `Partial`, and `Required` from 'typescript'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in multiple named exports from the 'typescript' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing TypeScript utilities
import { type, interface, Record, Partial, Required } from 'typescript';
steps.seedCode: // Import the TypeScript types and utilities here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary TypeScript type utilities imported for building typed test utilities.
successCriteria: The imports for type, interface, Record, Partial, and Required from 'typescript' are present.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the essential TypeScript type utilities needed for building typed test factories.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some imports are missing. Make sure to import all five: type, interface, Record, Partial, and Required from 'typescript'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or incomplete. Please import type, interface, Record, Partial, and Required from 'typescript'.

steps.title: Define the TestCase interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'TestCase' with three properties: 'description' (string), 'input' (any), and 'expected' (any).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the TypeScript types and utilities here

// Create the TestCase interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TestCase interface that defines the structure for test cases in your utility.
successCriteria: The TestCase interface is defined with description (string), input (any), and expected (any) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the TestCase interface with the correct properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface has all three required properties with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface isn't quite right. Check that you used the 'interface' keyword and defined all three properties.

steps.title: Define the TestResult interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named TestResult with three properties: description (string), passed (boolean), and error (optional string).
steps.hint: Use the interface keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TestResult interface is defined with the correct property types.
successCriteria: The TestResult interface exists with description: string, passed: boolean, and error?: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the TestResult interface with proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure all three properties (description, passed, error) are included with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TestResult interface isn't defined correctly. Check that you used the interface keyword and proper type annotations.

steps.title: Create the testRunner function signature
steps.instruction: Create a function signature for testRunner that takes an array of TestCase objects and returns an array of TestResult objects. Use proper TypeScript typing for the parameters and return type.
steps.hint: Define a function named testRunner with typed parameters and return type. The function should accept TestCase[] and return TestResult[].
steps.expectedOutcome: A properly typed testRunner function signature is added to the code.
successCriteria: The testRunner function is defined with correct parameter type (TestCase[]) and return type (TestResult[]).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the testRunner function signature with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure testRunner accepts TestCase[] and returns TestResult[] with proper type annotations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature doesn't match the requirements. Check that testRunner takes TestCase[] and returns TestResult[].

steps.title: Implement the testRunner function
steps.instruction: Implement the testRunner function body to process each test case and return a TestResult array.
steps.hint: Inside the testRunner function, use the testCases parameter and map each case to a TestResult object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The testRunner function should have a complete implementation that processes test cases.
successCriteria: testRunner function body is implemented and returns an array of TestResult objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the testRunner function with proper typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function returns TestResult[] and processes all test cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation is missing or incorrect. Check that the function body processes testCases and returns TestResult[].

steps.title: Create the createTestSuite factory function
steps.instruction: Create a function named createTestSuite that returns a test suite object with a run method.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object containing a run method. The run method should call testRunner with the provided test cases.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a createTestSuite function that returns an object with a run method, which internally uses testRunner.
successCriteria: The createTestSuite function is defined, returns an object with a run method, and the run method calls testRunner.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the typed test suite factory function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined createTestSuite, but make sure it returns an object with a run method that calls testRunner.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createTestSuite function is missing or doesn't match the expected structure. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Add runAllTests method to the factory
steps.instruction: Inside the createTestSuite function, add a runAllTests method to the returned object that calls testRunner with the stored test cases.
steps.hint: The method should be a function that returns the result of calling testRunner with the testCases parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createTestSuite factory function now returns an object with a runAllTests method that can execute all test cases.
successCriteria: The returned object from createTestSuite includes a runAllTests method that calls testRunner with the testCases parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the runAllTests method to the test suite factory.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the runAllTests method is properly defined inside the returned object and calls testRunner with testCases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The runAllTests method is missing or incorrectly implemented. Check that it's added to the returned object and properly calls testRunner.

steps.title: Add addTestCase method to the factory
steps.instruction: Inside the object returned by createTestSuite, add a method named addTestCase that takes a single testCase parameter of type TestCase and returns void.
steps.hint: The method should push the new test case into the existing testCases array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createTestSuite factory now returns an object with an addTestCase method that can add individual test cases.
successCriteria: The returned object includes an addTestCase method with correct parameter type and void return type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the addTestCase method to your test suite factory.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure addTestCase has the correct parameter type (TestCase) and returns void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addTestCase method is missing or has incorrect syntax. Check the method signature and placement.

steps.title: Create a sample test suite instance
steps.instruction: Create a sample test suite instance by calling createTestSuite with an empty array and assigning it to a variable named sampleSuite.
steps.hint: Use the createTestSuite factory function you built earlier. Pass an empty array as the initial test cases.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an instance of a factory function
const calculator = createCalculator();
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a sample test suite instance ready to use in the next step.
successCriteria: A variable named sampleSuite is declared and assigned the result of calling createTestSuite with an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a sample test suite instance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createTestSuite with an empty array and assigning it to a variable named sampleSuite.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to create a sample test suite instance by calling createTestSuite with an empty array.

steps.title: Run tests and display results
steps.instruction: Call the runAllTests method on your test suite instance and store the results in a typed variable.
steps.hint: Use the test suite instance you created earlier and call its runAllTests method. Assign the return value to a variable with the appropriate type annotation.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: calling a method and storing typed results
const results: TestResult[] = myTestSuite.runAllTests();
steps.expectedOutcome: The test suite executes and returns typed results that can be inspected.
successCriteria: The runAllTests method is called on the test suite instance and the results are stored in a properly typed variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully executed the test suite and captured the typed results.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling runAllTests on your test suite instance and storing the results with proper type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test execution isn't complete. Check that you're calling the runAllTests method on your test suite instance and assigning the results to a typed variable.
